limitations: This is a source-snapshot browser correctness ledger, not a release-wide parity claim or performance comparison.
Headless Chrome 152 on macOS arm64 only. Safari, Firefox, mobile hardware, and full application workloads were not exercised.
Vitest uses development runtime branches. The streamed CSS harness and the second security run use production bundles; native production transition behavior was not separately tested here.
The three Redact-only native cases assert its synchronous contract and are not counted as shared React parity.
Native resource tests combine real controlled image/font requests with injected decode and rejection conditions. They do not measure real-world network performance.
DNS/preconnect tests inspect emitted hints and deduplication, not whether Chrome chooses to open a network connection.
Trusted Types coverage is TrustedHTML client/hydration and iframe srcDoc, plus nonce hydration. It is not an exhaustive CSP sink audit and does not directly exercise TrustedScriptURL resource sinks.
Snapshot names, callbacks, CSS state, and browser animation handles are asserted. Visual animation quality was not reviewed with screenshots.
Passing these cases does not establish concurrent scheduling parity, which Redact intentionally downgrades.
